fixes.correction: Keep this composition: Nagoji straightened at the laterite parapet in the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat and silver chain, one hand on the stone, and two separate grey smoke columns far apart on the horizon. Both coat sleeves stay down to the wrists with the same white turned-back cuffs as in panel 1.1. Show no bare forearm, and no brand, scar, tattoo, mark or symbol of any kind on his arms or hands. The sentry must be the same man as in panel 1.1, and he is the only guard. He is bare-headed with long black hair in a topknot, with no turban and no head cloth, a thick moustache and a clean-shaven chin with no beard. He wears a white mundu with crossed leather belts and now stands straight with his spear held upright, no longer leaning. Nagoji keeps the grey at his temples, the small gold ear stud and a clean-shaven chin and jaw with no stubble.
fixes.issues: Nagoji's left coat sleeve is rolled to mid-forearm, which contradicts the closed cuffs in 1.1. On the bare forearm the brand is painted as a crisp dark emblem, a star or cross-like glyph, plus a scar, and it sits on the outer forearm. The bible requires a pale puckered patch blurred past reading, never a symbol and never on the outer forearm. The script does not call for the brand here at all. The sentry also changes from 1.1: he now wears a white turban and a full beard, where in 1.1 he was bare-headed with a topknot and a clean chin. A second guard has also been added. The two separate smoke columns and Nagoji's face are good.

fixes.correction: Render in the same inked comic line art with flat painted colour as panels 1.1 to 1.3: clean black outlines, no photographic or 3D-render look, no heavy depth-of-field blur except the soft foreground stick. The runner must be the same man as in panel 1.3. He has short curly black hair with no topknot, a thin moustache and a clean-shaven chin. He is bare-chested and slick with sweat, with no shoulder cloth, strap or satchel, and wears only a short plain white cloth tucked at the waist. He is barefoot, down on one knee, panting, with one palm flat on the floor. Use the same war hall as in 1.3: dark carved wooden pillars, warm interior light and brass standing lamps with open flames, with the sunlit open main doorway he ran through behind him. Frame low and tight on the runner so the map table, the dais and Varma's seat are out of frame, with no empty throne and no other figure. In the soft-focus left foreground show only the bottom of Padmini's walking stick, rough unpolished dark-brown natural wood as on her sheet with no brass ferrule. Hold it clearly an inch above the floor, with a visible gap and its small shadow below. Leave plain floor or dark wall at the top of the frame for two balloons.
fixes.issues: This panel is a photoreal 3D render with heavy depth of field, which clashes with the inked comic style of 1.1 to 1.3. The runner does not match 1.3: he has a topknot, a beard, a shoulder cloth over his chest, a cross strap and two satchels, where 1.3 shows short curly hair, a clean chin and a bare chest. The hall has also changed: plaster walls, slit windows and a side doorway. Varma's dais and seat are visible and empty, which breaks continuity. The stick has a polished brass ferrule and seems to touch the floor, unlike Padmini's rough natural staff held an inch above it.

fixes.correction: Frame close on Padmini from the chest up, filling the left and centre of a wide frame. She turns slowly toward the runner off-panel to the right, calm and level-eyed, with grey through her black hair coiled at the nape, simple gold, a cream sari with a gold border and her walking stick. Render the men behind her soft and out of focus, but keep them on model. Nagoji has clear grey streaks at the temples as in panels 1.1 to 1.3, a small gold ear stud, a curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin. Ramayyan has receding hair and plain white cloth. Varma has black hair with no grey in a side knot above his left ear, no topknot on the crown, is bare-chested and wears gold necklaces. Add no extra attendants or guards. Leave the runner off-panel. If any part of him shows at the right edge, he is bare-chested and sweat-slick with short curly black hair, no head cloth or tunic, and clean skin with no red marks, cuts or wounds. Keep a band of plain, dim hall wall across the upper part of the frame, clear of faces, for two balloons.
fixes.issues: The foreground runner has red smears on his upper arm that read as blood, which breaks the no-blood rule. He also wears a head cloth and a coarse tunic, where in 1.3 he is bare-chested. Nagoji has lost the grey at his temples that he shows in 1.1 to 1.3 and that the ch25-27 row requires, and his ear stud reads silver. Varma now has grey temples and a topknot on his crown instead of black hair in a side knot above his left ear, which makes him look like the older Nagoji. Extra attendants and guards appear that were not in 1.3. The script beat is missed: this is a medium group shot with every man sharp, not a close-up on Padmini with the men soft and blurred.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition, camera angle, lighting and both likenesses exactly as they are: Nagoji leaning over the table at left with one finger on the cloth map where the path narrows, Ramayyan seated across the table at right holding a stylus and a palm-leaf bundle, and the map drawn in ink lines only with no lettering. Change only these points. Nagoji's white coat sleeves stay buttoned down to the wrist on both arms, so no skin of the forearm shows: no brand, no scar, and no glyph, symbol, letter, numeral or tattoo-like mark anywhere on him. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble dots. Turn the background toward carved pillars and a plain shadowed wall so the royal dais and throne are out of frame. Keep the band above both heads as low-detail wall or shadowed roof so two speech balloons can sit there without touching either face.
fixes.issues: The brand on Nagoji's bared left forearm is drawn as a crisp dark glyph that looks like an '&' or an '8' with a tail. It reads as a legible tattooed symbol, which is pseudo-text and breaks the bible rule (a pale blurred burn, no legible letters or numerals). It sits right beside the key action, the pointing finger, so the letterer cannot cover it. Secondary problems: light stubble dots on his chin and jaw, and an empty royal throne in the centre background, although Varma is on his platform in 2.4. Everything else works: both likenesses (topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, breeches and boots; Ramayyan with stylus and palm leaves), the finger on an unlettered ink map, and the hall setting.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition, hall, lighting and Nagoji's pose exactly: Nagoji in the left foreground leaning over the unlettered ink map with his eyes on it and a troubled frown, and Marthanda Varma behind at right, standing on his raised platform and leaning forward with both hands on its edge. Redraw Varma strictly from the V13 varma-v1 sheet: his lean, older face with sharp cheekbones and a finer moustache with upturned tips, clearly a different man from Nagoji. He is bare-headed with his long black hair tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear, exactly as in page 1 panel 3. No crown topknot and no hair band. Keep him bare-chested in a cream mundu with a gold border, with gold necklaces and his spear beside him. Nagoji's white coat sleeves stay buttoned to the wrist on both arms so no forearm marks show, and his chin is smooth and clean-shaven. Any background guards wear white mundu with crossed leather belts, with no turbans and no red sashes. Keep the upper band of roof shadow and plain wall between and above the two heads low-detail for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: Varma does not match his sheet or the chapter row. His hair is in a crown topknot with a gold band, the same arrangement as Nagoji's, instead of the side knot above his left ear seen in 1.3. His face is younger and broader, with the same heavy curled moustache as Nagoji, so the two men read as near twins in the same panel. The V13 Varma has a leaner, older face and a finer upturned moustache. Nagoji's bared left forearm also shows a red, cross-like brand blotch, which breaks the 'not a cross' rule, and his jaw has light stubble. The background guards wear white turbans and red sashes instead of the Travancore white mundu with crossed leather belts. The composition, the hall and Nagoji's downward, troubled look at the map all work.

fixes.correction: Recompose as a true close-up in this wide strip. Nagoji's head and shoulders fill most of the panel height and sit in the left-centre third, three-quarter view facing frame right, eyes lowered, his fist pressed against his lips. Keep exactly the troubled expression, likeness and costume of the current image: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain of office. His coat sleeves stay buttoned to the wrist so no forearm marks show. Light him with a hard raking side light from a narrow vertical window slit just behind his shoulder at frame right, leaving the far side of his face in shadow. Through that slit, two faint grey smudges of smoke on the distant horizon. Fill the rest of the frame with plain shadowed stone wall, low in detail, so a caption at upper left and a short speech balloon near his mouth can sit without touching his face or hand. No guards, no other figures, no throne or daybed, and no text.
fixes.issues: The framing misses the script. 2.5 asks for a tight shot on Nagoji, lit from the side, with the smoke seen through a window slit behind him. This is a medium-wide room shot: his head fills only about 40 percent of the height, the light is flat daylight and the smoke shows through a large opening off to the right. Two background guards wear rust-red turbans with broad red sashes. That is Nagoji's old commander look, not the Travancore white mundu with crossed belts, and it does not match the white-turbaned guards in 2.4. Varma's red daybed sits empty with his spear, although he is present in 2.4. Nagoji himself is right: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, coat, waistcoat and chain, the fist-to-mouth brooding expression, and only light stubble.

fixes.correction: Keep the composition and pose: Nagoji alone in focus, leaning over the map table in the same war hall, right index finger tracing a thin zig zag along the canal, left palm flat on the cloth map. Keep him as drawn: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat hanging open over a red waistcoat with brass buttons, silver chain of office, knee breeches, no belt or buckle over the waistcoat. His inner LEFT forearm shows only a pale, puckered patch of raised scar tissue, lighter than his skin, with no dark outline or ink. It has no crescent, eye, spiral, symbol or tattoo shape. Beside it runs one long thin white scar from wrist toward elbow, and there are no other marks on his arms. The cloth map is ink lines only (canal, dotted path, ridges, tiny tree marks), with no letters, words, numerals, labels or letter-like squiggles anywhere, especially near his finger. Background: only two or three Nair guards at the doorways in white mundu, white head cloth and a crossed leather belt. Do not draw anyone in a red turban or broad red sash, anyone in ochre or indigo, or any other man with a topknot, curled moustache and gold ear stud. Either keep Varma's dais out of frame, or show Varma seated on it (bare-chested, gold necklaces, spear beside him). Leave the plain upper wall to the right of his head clear for two balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 (only candidate): the brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm, which sits at the centre of the panel as he leans on it, is drawn as a dark-outlined crescent or eye-shaped tattoo symbol, not the bible's pale puckered patch. The map has several tiny letter-like scribbles (pseudo-labels) right beside his pointing finger and among the hills. The background is crowded with extras who double Nagoji: a guard in a rust-red turban, cream tunic and broad red sash (his old commander look), and two men with his topknot, curled moustache and gold ear stud. There is also a man in an ochre tunic with an indigo sash who reads as a raider. A cushioned dais with a spear beside it stands empty behind him, though Varma sits there in 3.1 and 4.1. A leather belt with a brass buckle is strapped over his waistcoat. Face, topknot, grey temples, clean chin, stud and the pointing gesture are good.

fixes.correction: Keep everything that works in this frame: the two-shot across the map table in the same war hall, Padmini at left standing with her long stick (grey threading through black hair coiled at the nape, cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape with no blouse, gold earrings and necklace) glaring at Nagoji, and Nagoji at right straightening from the table to face her (Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office, breeches and boots). Keep the plain wall between the pillars clear for balloons. Fix one thing: Nagoji has NO tattoo and no dark ink, spiral, circle, glyph, letter or symbol anywhere on his skin. The old brand on his inner LEFT forearm is only a pale, puckered patch of raised scar tissue, lighter than his skin and without any outline, beside one long thin white scar from wrist toward elbow. It is acceptable to turn that forearm so the inner side faces away, or let the coat sleeve cover it. The red banner stays plain cloth with no device or writing.
fixes.issues: v01 (only candidate): Nagoji's inner left forearm, clearly visible on the chair back at frame right, carries a dark ink tattoo of a spiral-over-circle glyph that reads as a script letter or symbol. This breaks the no-pseudo-text rule and the bible's brand description (pale puckered patch, no letters, no symbol). Everything else works: the two-shot across the map table, Padmini with her stick, grey threading and cream gold-bordered sari with the old drape, Nagoji turning to face her with a correct face, stud, clean chin and uniform, the same hall and lamps as 3.1, a map with no lettering, a plain red banner, and clear wall between the pillars for three balloons.

fixes.correction: Show Marthanda Varma alone, standing at the front edge of his low platform (the same low platform with the cushioned seat seen on page 3). The platform sits right at the far end of the waist-high wooden map table, and he leans down so his spear tip runs along the canal line of the cloth map toward the fort marks. Keep his face, black hair in the side knot, cream gold-bordered mundu, gold necklaces and the clean ink-line map exactly as drawn. Draw NO other people at or around the table: no seated councillors, no men sitting on the floor, no turbaned, maroon-turbaned, bald or bearded onlookers. At most two small Nair guards in white mundu with crossed leather belts may stand far back by the main doorway, as on page 3. His eyes glance sideways past the frame edge toward the off-panel Nagoji and Padmini. Keep the upper third (roof beams and plain back wall) clear and low in detail for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: Varma's face, side knot, mundu, necklaces and the unlettered ink-line map with fort marks are right, and the spear tip on the canal works. But the hall is suddenly full of about eight unscripted councillors sitting on the floor around a low table (white and maroon turbans, grey beards), plus extra guards. Page 3 and 4.3 show only the principals, a waist-high map table and one or two distant guards. Varma is standing on the floor at the table, not on his platform, and he is looking at a seated stranger instead of between the off-panel Nagoji and Padmini.

fixes.correction: Keep Padmini exactly as drawn: face, grey-threaded coiled hair, gold, cream gold-bordered sari and walking stick. Frame her knees-up in three-quarter view, her head and shoulders turning sharply toward the right edge of the frame, where the king sits off-panel on his platform. Put the side wall, a carved pillar and a doorway behind her so the empty platform is NOT visible. Draw NO other people: no seated men, no councillors on the floor, no bald, turbaned or bearded onlookers. If the map table shows at all, it is the waist-high wooden table of page 3 with palm-leaf bundles and the unlettered ink-line map. Keep the upper area of plain wall clear and low in detail for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: Padmini matches her sheet and the ch26 row (grey threading in coiled hair, simple gold, cream gold-bordered sari, stick). The beat fails, though. Varma's platform is plainly visible behind her and EMPTY, so she cannot read as turning to face the king. Instead she is looking at a row of unscripted seated men (bearded, bald, topknotted) who fill both foreground corners. None of them appear on page 3, and the low floor-level council table does not match it either.

fixes.correction: Keep Padmini exactly as drawn: the pose, the stick coming down hard on the floor with small impact lines, her grey-threaded coiled hair, gold, cream gold-bordered sari and wet, furious eyes. Keep the wide 3:1 strip of the same hall. Remove the three seated foreground men and the row of guards: draw NO bearded, bald, turbaned or maroon-clad men anywhere. The three men she addresses (the king, Ramayyan and Nagoji) are off-panel on the camera side, so she faces toward the viewer and her glare sweeps across the foreground. At most two small Nair guards in white mundu with crossed leather belts may stand by the far doorway. The map table is the waist-high wooden table of page 3, with palm-leaf bundles and the unlettered ink-line cloth map. Keep the upper band (roof beams and dark back wall) clear and low in detail for three speech balloons, away from her face and the stick.
fixes.issues: Padmini and her stick strike, with impact lines, are good. But the 'three men' she faces are three invented strangers in the foreground: a bearded man in maroon cloth, a bald man and a bearded curly-haired man seen from behind. None of them is Varma, Ramayyan or Nagoji, so the beat reads wrong. A line of extra guards also fills the background, which does not match page 3.

fixes.correction: Keep Nagoji exactly as drawn: face, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw, grey at the temples, Kerala topknot, tiny flush gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office. Frame him as a medium shot from the waist up in the same hall, head dipped in one small nod, jaw set, throat tight. Remove every seated onlooker in the foreground: no turbaned, maroon-turbaned, bald or bearded men. At most one or two standing Nair guards may stay far back by a pillar, and Varma may remain small and soft-focus on his low platform in the background, as drawn. Both coat sleeves stay down to the wrists, so no forearm scar or brand shows. Keep the upper right (roof and back wall) clear and low in detail for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch26 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, Kerala topknot, small gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, breeches and boots. Varma on his platform in the background is right. But the foreground is crowded with unscripted seated onlookers (white turban, maroon turban, bald topknot, bearded men). That clashes with page 3, with 4.3 and with the crowd-free corrections for 4.1, 4.2 and 4.4. His pushed-up left sleeve shows a white scar drawn as two crossing lines, an X, which goes against the bible's 'not a cross' brand. The full-figure framing also weakens the tight-throat nod.

fixes.correction: Kayal, the bay mare Nagoji rides at the head of the column, must have NO white markings anywhere. Her face is solid ochre red-brown from forelock to muzzle, with no star, stripe, blaze or snip. She has a black mane, tail and lower legs and an ochre quilted saddle pad, exactly as on her sheet. Keep everything else in this composition unchanged: Nagoji at the head in the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, boots, silver chain and talwar, with Kerala topknot, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache and small gold ear stud; Ponnan half a length behind on his left on the smaller horse, with his spear and red shoulder cloth; the Travancore riders with crossed leather belts under the red silver-conch standard; the dry red road, the greasy smoke columns and sparks ahead, and the open sky at the top left for the two captions.
fixes.issues: v01 is strong on everything except Kayal. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch26 uniform row: topknot, grey temples, clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, chain, breeches, boots and talwar. Ponnan is half a length behind on Nagoji's left with his spear, red shoulder cloth, short jacket and bare knees. The Travancore riders have crossed belts under the red conch standard, and there is smoke with sparks ahead and open sky for both captions. The problem is that Kayal, the large foreground horse, has a clear white star and a faint stripe on her forehead. The Kayal sheet and the bible say plainly that she has no white markings. Kayal shows no marking in 5.2 and 5.3, so the star would also break continuity across this page.

fixes.correction: Reframe as a true close-up. Press the oil-soaked torch head against the dry leaves and bark at the base of one wooden vine support post. Put Nagoji's face close behind and just above the torch, lit warm orange from below by the torch flame, eyes fixed on the point of contact, waiting. The flame only touches: it is the torch's own small flame and nothing has caught yet, so no fire climbs the post, the leaf litter is not burning and no embers spread. Nagoji's chin and jaw are completely clean-shaven, with no stubble, stipple or beard shadow; he has a thick curled moustache, a small gold ear stud, a Kerala topknot and grey at the temples. The white coat sleeve stays down over the wrist of the hand holding the torch, so no scar or mark shows on that arm (his brand and scar are only on the inner LEFT forearm). Keep the daylight pepper garden with green vines and fruit, the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Leave clear, soft background (sky or blurred vines) in the upper-left quarter for the caption.
fixes.issues: v01 has four problems. (1) Nagoji has visible stubble and beard shadow on his chin and jaw, which breaks the clean-shaven rule; stubble is allowed only in captivity. (2) The white scar shows on the outer forearm of his near, right arm, but the bible puts it on the inner LEFT forearm. (3) The beat is not met. The script asks for a tight shot with Nagoji's face behind the torch, lit orange. Here it is a medium crouch with his face off to the left in flat daylight, not behind the torch. (4) A tall flame climbs the bark of the post and the leaf litter glows, so the fire reads as already caught. That spoils the 'nothing happened' page turn the script holds back.

fixes.correction: Keep this exact composition, setting, lighting and staging. In the foreground left, Nagoji runs toward the viewer's left: soot streaks on his face, Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, sooty white European coat, red waistcoat with brass buttons, silver chain of office, knee breeches and buckled boots. With one hand he hauls a coughing Travancore man (white mundu, crossed leather belts) back out of the smoke by his shoulder cloth. Coughing, stumbling raider silhouettes, arms over their faces, stay in the grey smoke behind, with the shrine, canal and pepper boats at left and smoky open sky across the top. Change only his arms: both white coat sleeves come down to his wrists, sooty but NOT rolled up, so neither bare forearm shows. Paint no white lines, scribbles, scratches, scars, tattoos or marks on either forearm or the back of either hand. The old brand and long white scar sit only on the INNER left forearm and are hidden under the sleeve in this panel. Nothing resembling handwriting, letters or symbols anywhere on skin or cloth. The raiders in the smoke wear dark indigo or earth-brown cloth and head cloths, with bare shoulders.
fixes.issues: The only candidate has a defect I would not print. Nagoji's bare left forearm, the arm hauling the man, carries a white jagged scrawl on its OUTER, upper surface. At full size it looks like cursive handwriting, which counts as pseudo-text in the art. It also breaks the bible: the brand and scar belong only on the INNER left forearm, never the outer forearm. Everything else works: soot-streaked face, clean chin, moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples, sooty white coat, red waistcoat, chain, breeches and boots. He hauls a Travancore man in a crossed belt by the shoulder cloth while raiders cough and stumble in the smoke with arms over their faces. There are no bodies, and the sky at top centre has room for both captions.

fixes.correction: Keep this exact composition, night lamplight and placement: Varma on his low platform at the far end, sooty soldiers in white mundu sitting along the walls, the map table at left, Nagoji seated in the right-centre foreground lowering a brass cup from his lips with a grimace, and Padmini entering through the side doorway at frame right with her stick. Fix the following. Nagoji's white coat sleeves are worn DOWN to the wrists with soot-blackened cuffs, so no forearm skin shows on either arm. No tattoos, circles, symbols, scars or marks anywhere on his hands or wrists; his brand and scar are on the LEFT forearm and stay hidden under the sleeve in this panel. Padmini has no forehead mark and a clean, smooth upper lip with no shadow that could read as hair. Her grey-threaded black hair is coiled at the nape and damp at the temples. Put the soot streaks on the lower half and hem of her cream sari and keep the drape over her shoulder clean. Varma is bare-headed with his hair gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, with no loose curls and no turban. Varma, the soldiers and Nagoji's eyes all turn toward Padmini at the door.
fixes.issues: Nagoji's coat sleeves are pushed up to the elbows. His RIGHT forearm, the one holding the cup, next to his face, shows a dark ring mark like a tattoo plus a white scar, and his left forearm shows another scar. That puts a brand-like mark on the wrong arm. The bible row puts the brand and scar on the inner LEFT forearm only, and the brand is a pale puckered patch, not a dark symbol. Padmini has a white vertical forehead mark that is not on her sheet, and a dark upper-lip shadow that reads like a faint moustache. Varma's hair hangs in loose curls instead of the side knot above his left ear. Otherwise the composition is strong and on beat.

fixes.correction: Keep the waist-high two-shot across the map table, with the ink-line map (no lettering), palm-leaf bundles, brass lamps and warm night lamplight. Keep Padmini standing unmoving with her stick and her hard, flat stare. Keep Nagoji's open-palm answering gesture and his look: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office. Change the following. Mirror the staging so Nagoji stands on the LEFT of the table facing right and Padmini on the RIGHT facing left. Nagoji's coat sleeves are DOWN to the wrists with soot-blackened cuffs and no bare forearm. No glyph, symbol, tattoo, letter-like mark or scar is drawn on any skin. Varma is present as a lamplit figure on his low platform in the background behind Padmini: bare-headed, hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, bare-chested, cream mundu with a gold border, gold necklaces. The royal seat is never empty. The background soldiers match the previous wide: sooty Travancore men in white mundu with crossed leather belts, bare-headed, sitting quietly along the walls, with no turbans, no red turbans and no red sashes.
fixes.issues: Nagoji's bare left forearm has a dark, letter-like glyph that looks like a tattoo, plus a pink scar line. That is pseudo-text in the art, and it contradicts the bible's brand: a pale puckered patch with no letters and no symbols. Varma's platform in the background is an empty seat with a red cushion, which contradicts 7.3, where Varma sits on it. The guards wear red turbans and red sashes with no cross-belts, unlike the bare-headed sooty soldiers of 7.2. The staging is also flipped: Padmini is on the left and Nagoji on the right, against 7.2's geography, where Padmini is on the right, and 7.5, where Nagoji looks toward frame right.

fixes.correction: Keep this exact composition, the laterite wall walk, the tiled tower and the guards beside it, the sunset light, the dark burned strip on the horizon, Nagoji's pose leaning on the parapet and both costumes unchanged. Fix only Revathi's hair. Under the chapter 20-28 continuity she now has grey threading through her black hair, drawn as in the neighbouring panels: a clearly visible silver-grey streak sweeping back from the temple above her visible ear into the braid, plus a few fine grey strands through the black at the crown. Her face stays the age on her sheet (a little younger than Nagoji), not elderly. Keep the jasmine in her braid, the sandalwood line at the hairline, the tali on its cord, the flat-coin necklace, the gold armlets and the deep indigo sari with gold.
fixes.issues: v01 is strong otherwise: right wall walk, sunset, the burned strip on the horizon, Nagoji alone at the parapet in the correct uniform (clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples), Revathi walking toward him, and open sky for both lettering lines. It fails the ch20-28 bible row for Revathi: her hair is solid black with no grey threading. Panels 9.2 and 9.3 on the same page show a clear grey streak at her temple, so this panel would break continuity on the page.

fixes.correction: Keep the laterite fort wall walk and parapet, the same sunset light and sky, the burned strip on the horizon, and Nagoji's face, Kerala topknot, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain of office. Fix the arms: both coat sleeves stay fully down to the wrists, with matching turned-back cuffs and brass buttons on each arm. Show no bare forearm, and no scar, cross, mark or brand anywhere on his arms or hands. Frame it tighter for a small panel, chest up. His head and shoulders turn toward frame right, and his gaze is level and sideways at close range on someone standing just beside him off-panel at frame right (Revathi, who stands to his right in 9.5), not out at the distant horizon. His expression is quiet and questioning, brows slightly drawn, lips just parted. One hand rests relaxed on the parapet; no fist on the hip. Leave clear open sky above and in front of his face for one balloon.
fixes.issues: v01 fails on three points. (1) His left coat sleeve is pushed back to show a bare forearm with a white CROSS-shaped mark on the outer forearm. The bible forbids the brand from reading as a cross, puts it on the inner forearm, and the script never calls for it here; the cuff also no longer matches his other sleeve. (2) He gazes into the distance with a fist on his hip, so he is not turned toward Revathi's profile at close range, and the swaggering pose does not fit the quiet question. (3) It is framed as a wide full-figure shot rather than a small panel.

Fix only Revathi's hair. Under the chapter 20-28 continuity she now has grey threading through her black hair, matching panels 9.2 and 9.3 on this page: a clearly visible silver-grey streak sweeping back from the temple above her visible ear into the braid, plus a few fine grey strands through the black at the crown. Her face stays the age on her sheet (a little younger than Nagoji), not elderly. Keep the jasmine braid, sandalwood line, tali, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and the deep indigo sari with gold.

fixes.correction: Nagoji is seen from behind at frame left, over his right shoulder. The silver chain of office passes over both shoulders and dips in a shallow loop across the upper back, with NO medallion or pendant on his back (the medallion hangs at his chest, out of view). Leave open sky across the top centre for two balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) gets the beat and Revathi right: she is a few paces off, turned back halfway in the last light, hand at the tali, with grey threading. Nagoji's foreground back view, which fills nearly half the frame, has front-of-coat features on its back. His coat is split open down the back, showing a wedge of red waistcoat with brass buttons, and the chain of office hangs in a V on his back with its medallion between the shoulder blades. It reads as a coat worn back to front, or a torso facing camera under a head turned away, and it breaks the ch25-27 uniform row.

fixes.correction: In the last attempt Ibrahim stood at frame left turned toward viewer's right, which showed his RIGHT ear and RIGHT jaw, and the scar landed on the wrong cheek in red. Mirror the staging. The shadowed man seen from behind stands at frame LEFT. Ibrahim stands at frame RIGHT, his body and face turned three-quarters toward viewer's LEFT as he speaks to that man, so his anatomical LEFT cheek, LEFT ear and the left side of his jaw face the camera. His scar is one thin PALE line, lighter than his skin and never red, from just below the LEFT ear lobe down to the jaw line on the side of his face nearest the camera, with no mark on the right cheek. Keep everything that worked: the dusk canal with a moored boat and roped cloth bales, the clay oil lamp, his white turban, short grey-flecked beard, muted teal short coat over the cream vest with bulging pockets, white mundu and blue-striped shoulder cloth, the open-handed confiding gesture, the other man in dark cloth and shadow, and a clear band of dusk sky across the upper frame for the two captions.
fixes.issues: The scar is on the wrong side. Ibrahim stands at frame left with his body to camera and his head turned toward viewer's right, so the ear and cheek nearest the camera (viewer's left of his face) are his RIGHT ones. The scar runs from that RIGHT ear to the jaw, and it is painted reddish instead of the thin pale line the prompt asks for. The script needs his anatomical LEFT side with the LEFT-ear-to-jaw scar clearly visible. Everything else is good: dusk canal, moored boat, roped cloth bales, white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over a cream vest with bulging pockets, sound hands, a shadowed man seen from behind, and clear dusk sky for the captions. A horizontal mirror of v01 would put the scar on the correct side, since the frame has no text.

Instead make an extreme close-up of the tabletop only, with NO faces and NO other people anywhere in the frame. Ramayyan's two thin, fine-boned brown hands enter from frame left with only the edge of his plain white cloth at the forearm. His left hand lifts and turns one blank palm leaf; his right hand holds the slender stylus, its point already pressed to the next leaf. At frame right a small brass dish of dried black peppercorns sits on top of a tied stack of finished blank palm leaves, weighing it down. The background is only a soft, dim blur of a timber pillar and laterite wall in the same midday daylight as panels 11.3 and 11.4. Keep the upper third of the strip as plain dark tabletop shadow or blurred wall for the two captions. Keep what worked: the blank palm leaves with no marks, the brass dish of black peppercorns, the warm wood table, the sound hands and the inked graphic-novel style.
